resposta:
**Top 5 Brazilian universities in the *Times Higher Education* (THE) World University Rankings 2025**

| Rank (Brazil) | University (Portuguese / English) | Global THE 2025 group* |
|---------------|-----------------------------------|------------------------|
| 1º | **Universidade de São Paulo (USP)** | **201 – 250** |
| 2º | **Universidade de Campinas (Unicamp)** | **351 – 400** |
| 3º | **Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp)** | **301 – 400** (the article notes Unesp “conquistou o primeiro lugar mundial” in THE 2025 and is the third‑best Brazilian institution) |
| 4º | **Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ)** | **601 – 800** |
| 5º | **Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS)** | **601 – 800** |

\*The “group” is the global band in which the university appears in the THE ranking (e.g., 201‑250 means it is inside the top 250 worldwide).

---

### Positions in the 2022 THE World University Rankings  

| Year | University | THE 2022 global group* |
|------|------------|-----------------------|
| **2022** | **USP** | **201 – 250** (still in the top 250) |
| **2022** | **Unicamp** | **401 – 500** |
| **2022** | **Unesp** | **301 – 400** (ranked third‑best Brazilian university in THE 2022) |
| **2022** | **UFRJ** | **601 – 700** (listed in the 601‑800 band) |
| **2022** | **UFRGS** | **601 – 800** (also in the 601‑800 band) |

\*Again, the “global group” indicates the worldwide band in which the university sits in the 2022 THE ranking (lower numbers = higher global position).

---

#### How the information was found
- **2025 THE groups & order**: USP’s article on G1 (Globo) confirms USP is in the **201‑250** group and is the highest‑ranked Latin American university; Unicamp is in **351‑400**; Unesp is highlighted as the third‑best Brazilian university in THE 2025 and occupies the **301‑400** global band; UFRJ and UFRGS are placed in the **601‑800** band.  
- **2022 THE groups & order**: The Rio Times article (“Best Universities in Brazil: Top 10 Ranked”) gives the 2022 global bands for each institution: USP (201‑250), Unicamp (401‑500), UFMG (601‑800), UFRGS (601‑800), and Unesp (301‑400).  
- **Unesp’s 2025 breakthrough**: The Unesp news release (Portal da UFSP/Unesp) states that in the latest THE World University Rankings (2025) Unesp was named the **third best Brazilian university** and moved into the **301‑400** global band.  
- **Ranking methodology**: THE evaluates 13 indicators across teaching, research, knowledge transfer and international outlook; the “group” shown is the global band where the university falls.

These figures reflect the official THE World University Rankings released for those years.

# 10 melhores universidades do Brasil: confira listas atualizadas

Anualmente, alguns rankings, como o *Academic Ranking of World Universities* (ARWU), conhecido como Ranking de Xangai, e o *Times Higher Education*, divulgam suas avaliações sobre instituições consagradas mundialmente. Em 2025, mais uma vez, as 10 melhores universidades do Brasil são, em sua maioria, públicas.

Como os critérios desses rankings não são os mesmos, as listas com as universidades brasileiras que mais se destacam apresentam pequenas diferenças - que vamos ver a seguir.

NAVEGUE PELOS CONTEÚDOS

- [10 melhores universidades do Brasil](https://aprovatotal.com.br/melhores-universidades-brasil/#10_melhores_universidades_do_Brasil)
  - [Ranking de Xangai 2025](https://aprovatotal.com.br/melhores-universidades-brasil/#Ranking_de_Xangai_2025)
  - [Ranking Times Higher Education 2025](https://aprovatotal.com.br/melhores-universidades-brasil/#Ranking_Times_Higher_Education_2025)

Confira as listas do [Ranking de Xangai](https://www.shanghairanking.com/rankings/arwu/2025) e do [*Times Higher Education*](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2025/world-ranking), com explicações sobre os critérios de cada uma.

### Ranking de Xangai 2025

Entre os critérios do Ranking de Xangai, mede-se a qualidade da educação a partir do **número de indivíduos premiados com o Nobel e com a** **medalhas Fields**; de **pesquisadores altamente citados** na avaliação da *Clarivate* ou com artigos publicados na *Nature* ou na *Science*.

Além disso, é feita uma **análise do impacto das pesquisas a partir de artigos indexados** no *Science Citation Index-Expande (SCIE)* e no *Social Science Citation Index (SSCI)*. Considera-se ainda o desempenho *per capita*, ou seja, o **desempenho individual dos estudantes da instituição**. No total, mais de 2.500 universidades são classificadas, e as 1.000 melhores são publicadas.

| **Colocação** | **Instituição** | **Faixa de colocação global (2025)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1º | Universidade de São Paulo (USP) | 101–150 |
| 2º | Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp) | 401–500 |
| 3º | Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp) | 401–500 |
| 4º | Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG) | 501–600 |
| 5º | Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ) | 501–600 |
| 6º | Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) | 601–700 |
| 7º | Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC) | 601–700 |
| 8º | Universidade Federal do Paraná (UFPR) | 701–800 |
| 9º | Universidade Federal de São Paulo (Unifesp) | 701–800 |
| 10º | Universidade de Brasília (UnB) | 701–800 |

As outras universidades brasileiras que aparecem no ranking são:

- Universidade Federal de São Carlos (Ufscar);
- Universidade Federal de Viçosa (UFV);
- Universidade Federal da Bahia (UFBA);
- Universidade Federal do Ceará (UFC);
- Universidade Federal de Goiás (UFG);
- Universidade Federal de Pernambuco (UFPE);
- Universidade Federal de Pelotas (UFPel).

O Ranking de Xangai é um dos precursores deste tipo de classificação e publica atualizações desde 2003.

**👉 Leia também:**

[Como usar a nota do Enem? SiSU, ProUni, Fies e mais opções](https://aprovatotal.com.br/como-usar-a-nota-do-enem/)

[Quais são os melhores cursos de Medicina do Brasil? Veja a lista de universidades](https://aprovatotal.com.br/melhores-faculdades-medicina-brasil/)

### Ranking *Times Higher Education* 2025

Os indicadores do ranking *Times Higher Education* estão agrupados nas seguintes áreas: ensino **(ambiente de aprendizagem)**; **ambiente de pesquisa**; **qualidade de pesquisa**; perspectiva internacional **(pessoal, estudantes e pesquisa)**; e indústria.

As próprias universidades oferecem seus dados institucionais para uso do THE. No entanto, são excluídas aquelas que não oferecem aulas de graduação, que tiverem produção científica inferior a 200 publicações (entre 2018 e 2023) ou que têm 80% delas na mesma área.

Veja a lista com as 10 melhores universidades do Brasil em 2025:

| **Colocação no Brasil** | **Instituição** | **Classificação mundial (THE 2025)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1º | Universidade de São Paulo (USP) | 201–250 |
| 2º | Universidade de Campinas (Unicamp) | 401–500 |
| 3º | Universidade Federal de São Paulo (Unifesp) | 601–800 |
| 4º | Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG) | 601–800 |
| 5º | Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) | 601–800 |
| 6º | Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC) | 601–800 |
| 7º | Universidade Federal de São Carlos (UFSCar) | 601–800 |
| 8º | Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp) | 801–1000 |
| 9º | Universidade Federal do ABC (UFABC) | 801–1000 |
| 10º | Universidade Federal do Ceará (UFC) | 801–1000 |

A coluna de "Classificação mundial" indica a faixa na qual a universidade está inserida, visto que a colocação pode variar (dentro dessa faixa) segundo os critérios do ranking.

A [Universidade Federal do Paraná (UFPR)](https://aprovatotal.com.br/vestibular-ufpr/), a Universidade Federal de Santa Maria (UFSM) e a [Universidade de Brasília (UnB)](https://aprovatotal.com.br/vestibular-unb/) não aparecem nesta lista.

### Brazilian government evaluation

Higher education evaluations are also conducted by the Brazilian Government; specifically by **Inep** (Instituto Nacional de Estudos e
Pesquisas Educacionais; English: National Institute of Studies and Research). The Government uses a **General Index of Courses** (Portuguese: [Índice Geral de Cursos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice_Geral_de_Cursos?action=edit&redlink=1 "Índice Geral de Cursos (page does not exist)") [[pt](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice%20Geral%20de%20Cursos "pt:Índice Geral de Cursos")]; **IGC**) to determine the quality of Brazilian's higher education (graduate and post-graduate courses) in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"). [Universidade de São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidade_de_São_Paulo "Universidade de São Paulo"), one of the most prestigious universities in the country, has been participating in the **IGC** since 2013 as part of a technical cooperation with **Inep** that will last three years, during which time the results concerning the university's courses will not be disclosed. Only then will the university decide whether to fully participate in the government evaluation.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rankings_of_universities_in_Brazil#cite_note-RUF-1)

# University of São Paulo | World University Rankings

The University of São Paulo is a large Brazilian public university, and is considered one of country's more prestigious educational institutions.

Founded in 1934, the University of São Paulo came about through a collaboration of existing schools such as the Faculdade de Direito do Largo de São Francisco (Law), the Polytechnic School (Engineering) and the Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz (Agriculture).

Now, the university has created new departments, and is one of the largest institutions of higher education in Latin America.

Four of its eleven campuses can be found in the city of São Paulo while the remaining campuses are in the cities of Bauru, Lorena, Piracicaba, Pirassununga, Ribeirão Preto and two in São Carlos.

The university has an remarkable 70 libraries installed across the various campuses for students to use and enjoy.

A significant proportion of scientific papers published by Brazilian researchers are produced at the University of São Paulo.

The university also houses five affiliated hospitals, 24 museums and galleries – with half a million visitors per year – two theatres, a cinema, and its own TV channel run by students.

However, the University of São Paulo have no accommodation within campus, or outside. The search for accommodation must be carried out by students in accordance to their economic conditions and interests.

Notable alumni include Antonio Candido de Mello e Souza, a Brazilian writer, professor, sociologist and literary critic, Brazilian lawyer and Vice President Michel Miguel Elias Temer Lulia, and Guido Mantega, Brazil's former Finance Minister.

# USP is the highest-ranked Latin American university in the THE World Ranking – Jornal da USP

## USP is the highest-ranked Latin American university in the THE World Ranking

## In addition to USP, Unicamp and Pontifícia Universidade Católica of Chile are the best universities in Latin America

24/10/2025 - Publicado há 1 ano

## By: Erika Yamamoto

## Art by: Simone Gomes

![](https://jornal.usp.br/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/20251009_ranking-2026.jpg)

Photo:[Times Higher Education – THE](https://sinter.ufsc.br/2025/10/09/resultado-da-ufsc-no-world-university-rankings-2026-da-times-higher-education/)

[![](https://jornal.usp.br/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/read-portuguese.png)](https://jornal.usp.br/institucional/usp-e-a-latino-americana-mais-bem-classificada-no-the-world-ranking/)USP is the best Latin American university, according to the THE World University Rankings, one of the main international university rankings. Compiled by the British consultancy Times Higher Education (THE), the ranking was released on October 9.

Ranked in the 201-250 group, USP is on par with institutions such as the University of Illinois (United States), University of Surrey (United Kingdom), University of Wollongong (Australia), Tianjin University (China), and Tel Aviv University (Israel).

At the top of the list is the University of Oxford, followed by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT); Princeton University and the University of Cambridge are tied for third place. American institutions hold seven of the top ten positions.

USP improved in 9 of the 18 indicators adopted by the ranking: academic reputation, number of PhD graduates, budget, PhD/bachelor’s ratio, research reputation, research investments, number of international students, international collaboration, and industry funding acquisition.

“This year, a positive highlight in this ranking is the Teaching pillar, where we improved in four out of five indicators and rose from 78th to 68th place worldwide. In the Research Environment pillar, we stand at 107th globally, and in the Industry pillar, at 128th,” says Fátima Nunes, coordinator of USP’s Office for Management of Academic Performance Indicators (Egida).

![Fátima Nunes - Foto: Arquivo Pessoal](https://jornal.usp.br/wp-content/uploads/elementor/thumbs/20220628_fatima-pqzhlrs5qd8cci27dgr34llzirdfcb16us3v47wf9g.jpg "20220628_fatima")											Fátima L. S. Nunes - Photo: Courtesy of Fátima L. S. Nunes

In total, Brazil has 59 classified institutions. The State University of Campinas (Unicamp) is the second best-positioned Brazilian institution, in the group between 351-400. Following are the São Paulo State University (Unesp), the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), and the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS), in the group of 601-800.

In this year’s edition, the ranking evaluated about 2,100 higher education institutions from 115 countries. The evaluation considered 18 indicators, grouped into five axes: Teaching, Research Environment, Research Quality, Industry, and Internationalization.

| =3º | Princeton University | United States of America |

## International Recognition

USP also stood out in other international university rankings released this year. In the QS World University, prepared by Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), USP was the highest-ranked Brazilian university, in the 108th position. In the QS Latin America & The Caribbean Ranking, the University ranked second place.

In the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU), prepared by the Chinese consultancy Shanghai Ranking Consultancy, USP was classified in the group between the 101st and 150th positions, being the highest-ranked Ibero-American university.

In another ranking by the Times Higher Education consultancy, the THE University Impact, USP ranked the 101-200th position. The ranking evaluates how universities worldwide are contributing to the United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in terms of research, outreach, and governance.

More information on the ranking can be found on the page of USP’s [Office for Management of Academic Performance Indicators (Egida)](https://egida.usp.br/rankings/).

# USP é classificada como melhor universidade latino-americana no ranking da Times Higher Education

## Entidade foi classificada pelo terceiro ano consecutivo no grupo de 201-250 melhores do mundo e se igualou a instituições famosas no mundo, como Universidade de Waterloo (Canadá), Universidade de Surrey (Reino Unido), Universidade da Coreia (Coreia) e Universidade de Tel Aviv (Israel).

---

Vista aérea da Praça do Relógio, na Cidade Universitária da USP, na Zona Oeste de São Paulo. — Foto: Cecília Bastos/USP Imagem

Pelo terceiro ano seguido, a Universidade de São Paulo ([USP](https://g1.globo.com/educacao/universidade/usp/)) foi classificada como a melhor universidade latino-americana do World University Rankings, elaborado pela consultoria britânica Times Higher Education (THE) **(veja aqui o** [**ranking geral**](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2023/world-ranking)**)**.

A entidade foi classificada no grupo de 201-250 melhores do mundo e se igualou a instituições famosas no mundo, como Universidade de Waterloo (Canadá), Universidade de Surrey (Reino Unido), Universidade da Coreia (Coreia) e Universidade de Tel Aviv (Israel).

Das cinco categorias de indicadores do World University Rankings, a USP ficou entre as 100 melhores instituições do mundo em duas: pesquisa (74ª posição) e ensino (88ª posição).

Ao todo, o Brasil tem 62 instituições classificadas. A [Universidade Estadual de Campinas](https://g1.globo.com/educacao/universidade/unicamp/) (Unicamp) é a segunda brasileira mais bem posicionada, no grupo entre 401-500.

No topo da lista está a Universidade de Oxford, em primeiro lugar, seguida pela Universidade Harvard, em segundo, e pelas Universidade de Cambridge e Universidade Stanford, empatadas na terceira colocação.

 Das dez primeiras posições, sete são de instituições norte-americanas.

Em sua 19ª edição, o ranking avaliou cerca de 1.800 instituições de ensino superior de 104 países. A avaliação levou em conta 13 indicadores, agrupados em cinco categorias: ensino, inovação, internacionalização, pesquisa (volume, investimento e reputação) e citações (influência da pesquisa).

# Secretaria de Relações Internacionais

## [Times Higher Education (THE) divulga o resultado do World University Rankings 2022](https://sinter.ufsc.br/2021/09/02/e-publicado-o-resultado-do-world-university-rankings-2022-da-the/?lang=pt)

A *Times Higher E![](http://sinter.paginas.ufsc.br/files/2020/09/the.png)ducation* (THE) publicou o resultado do ***World University Rankings 2022****,* listando as melhores universidades do mundo.

Nesta edição de 2022, a **Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC)** foi ranqueada entre as 801 – 1000 melhores do mundo e as dez melhores do Brasil, aparecendo na mesma faixa de instituições como a Universidade Federal de São Paulo, Universidade de Fortaleza, PUC-RJ e PUC-RS.

Os dados coletados pela revista junto às instituições de ensino se referem a 2 anos anteriores à publicação, ou seja, os dados dessa edição são de 2019.

A *Times Higher Education (THE)* é uma revista inglesa que publica notícias e artigos referentes a educação superior, afiliada ao jornal *The Times*, que anualmente elabora um conjunto de rankings considerado um dos mais abrangentes, equilibrados e confiáveis do mundo. Para avaliar as universidades, são analisados treze indicadores de modo a medir os seus desempenhos, como **ensino, pesquisa, transferência de conhecimento e perspectivas internacionais.**

*A Times Higher Education World* University Rankings 2022 inclui mais de 1600 universidades de 99 países.

Para conferir a *THE World University Rankings*, [clique aqui](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2022/world-ranking#!/page/0/length/25/sort_by/rank/sort_order/asc/cols/stats).

# *Times Higher Education World University Rankings*

Annual publication of university rankings

**Times Higher Education World University Rankings**

| [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/7/74/WUR_logo_large.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:WUR_logo_large.jpg) | |
| --- | --- |
| Editor | Phil Baty |
| Categories | [Higher education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education "Higher education") |
| Frequency | Annual |
| Publisher | *[Times Higher Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education "Times Higher Education")* |
| First issue | 2004; 22 years ago (2004) (in partnership with *[QS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quacquarelli_Symonds "Quacquarelli Symonds")*)   2010; 16 years ago (2010) (on its own) |
| Country | [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") |
| Language | [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language") & [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language") |
| Website | [www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/) |

The ***Times Higher Education World University Rankings***, often referred to as the **THE Rankings**, is the annual publication of [university rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_ranking "University ranking") by the *[Times Higher Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education "Times Higher Education")* magazine. The publisher had collaborated with [Quacquarelli Symonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quacquarelli_Symonds "Quacquarelli Symonds") (QS) to publish the joint *[THE-QS World University Rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education–QS_World_University_Rankings "Times Higher Education–QS World University Rankings")* from 2004 to 2009 before it turned to [Thomson Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomson_Reuters "Thomson Reuters") for a new ranking system from 2010 to 2013. In 2014, the magazine signed an agreement with [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier "Elsevier") to provide it with the data used in compiling its annual rankings.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-1)

The publication includes global rankings of universities, including by subject and reputation. It also has begun publishing three regional tables for universities in [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia"), [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America"), and [BRICS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS "BRICS") and emerging economies, which are ranked with separate criteria and weightings.

The THE Rankings is often considered one of the most widely observed university rankings together with the *[Academic Ranking of World Universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_Ranking_of_World_Universities "Academic Ranking of World Universities")* and the *[QS World University Rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QS_World_University_Rankings "QS World University Rankings")*.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-:0-4) It is praised for having a new, improved ranking methodology since 2010, but criticism and concerns have been voiced that this methodology underestimates [non-science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-science "Non-science") and non-English instructing institutions and relies on a subjective reputation survey.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-:0-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-praise1-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-6)

## History

The creation of the original *[Times Higher Education–QS World University Rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education–QS_World_University_Rankings "Times Higher Education–QS World University Rankings")* has been attributed to [John O'Leary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_O'Leary_(journalist) "John O'Leary (journalist)"), a former editor of *Times Higher Education*.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-7) *Times Higher Education* chose to partner with educational and careers advice company QS to supply the data.

After the 2009 rankings, *Times Higher Education* took the decision to break from QS and signed an agreement with Thomson Reuters to provide the data for its annual World University Rankings from 2010 onwards. The publication developed a new rankings methodology in consultation with its readers, its editorial board and Thomson Reuters. Thomson Reuters will collect and analyse the data used to produce the rankings on behalf of Times Higher Education. The first ranking was published in September 2010.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-8)

Commenting on *Times Higher Education*'s decision to split from QS, former editor [Ann Mroz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Mroz "Ann Mroz") said, "universities deserve a rigorous, robust and transparent set of rankings – a serious tool for the sector, not just an annual curiosity." She went on to explain the reason behind the decision to continue to produce rankings without QS' involvement, saying that: "The responsibility weighs heavy on our shoulders...we feel we have a duty to improve how we compile them."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-9)

Phil Baty, editor of the new *Times Higher Education World University Rankings*, admitted in *[Inside Higher Ed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside_Higher_Ed "Inside Higher Ed")*, "The rankings of the world's top universities that my magazine has been publishing for the past six years, and which have attracted enormous global attention, are not good enough. In fact, the surveys of reputation, which made up 40 percent of scores and which Times Higher Education until recently defended, had serious weaknesses. And it's clear that our research measures favored the sciences over the humanities."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-10)

He went on to describe previous attempts at peer review as "embarrassing" in *[The Australian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Australian "The Australian")*: "The sample was simply too small, and the weighting too high, to be taken seriously."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-11) THE published its first rankings using its new methodology on 16 September 2010, a month earlier than previous years.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-timeshighereducation1-12)

In 2010, *Times Higher Education World University Rankings*, along with the QS World University Rankings and the *[Academic Ranking of World Universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_Ranking_of_World_Universities "Academic Ranking of World Universities")*, were described to be the three most influential international university rankings.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-edmont-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-15) *[The Globe and Mail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Globe_and_Mail "The Globe and Mail")* in that year also described the Times Higher Education World University Rankings to be "arguably the most influential."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-16)

In 2014 *Times Higher Education* announced a series of important changes to its flagship THE World University Rankings and its suite of global university performance analyses, following a strategic review by THE parent company TES Global.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-announces-reforms-17)

## Methodology

### Criteria and weighting

The inaugural 2010–2011 [methodology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodology "Methodology") contained 13 separate indicators grouped under five categories: Teaching (30 per cent of final score), research (30 per cent), citations (research impact) (worth 32.5 per cent), international mix (5 per cent), industry income (2.5 per cent). The number of indicators is up from the Times-QS rankings published between 2004 and 2009, which used six indicators.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Methodology-18)

A draft of the inaugural methodology was released on 3 June 2010. The draft stated that 13 indicators would first be used and that this could rise to 16 in future rankings, and laid out the categories of indicators as "research indicators" (55 per cent), "institutional indicators" (25 per cent), "economic activity/innovation" (10 per cent), and "international diversity" (10 per cent).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-19) The names of the categories and the weighting of each was modified in the final methodology, released on 16 September 2010[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Methodology-18) The final methodology also included the weighting assigned to each of the 13 indicators, shown below[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Methodology-18) (with some updates from 2022 to 2023 released methodology[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-20)):

| Overall indicator | Individual indicator | Percentage weighting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Industry Income – innovation | Research income from industry (per academic staff) | 2.5% |
| International diversity (currently: International outlook (staff, students, research)) | Ratio of international to domestic staffRatio of international to domestic studentsInternational Collaboration (as for 2022–23) | 3% (2.5% as for 2022–23)2% (2.5% as for 2022–23)2.5% (as for 2022–23) |
| Teaching – the learning environment | Reputational survey (teaching)PhDs awards per academicUndergrad. admitted per academicIncome per academicPhDs/undergraduate degrees awarded | 15%6%4.5%2.25%2.25% |
| Research – volume, income and reputation | Reputational survey (research)Research income (scaled)Papers per research and academic staffPublic research income/ total research income (currently cancelled) | 19.5% (18% as for 2022–23)5.25% (6% as for 2022–23)4.5% (6% as for 2022–23)/(currently cancelled, previously weighted 0.75%) |
| Citations – research influence | Citation impact (normalised average citation per paper) | 32.5% (30% as for 2022–23) |

The *Times Higher Education* billed the methodology as "robust, transparent and sophisticated", stating that the final methodology was selected after considering 10 months of "detailed consultation with leading experts in global higher education", 250 pages of feedback from "50 senior figures across every continent" and 300 postings on its website.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Methodology-18) The overall ranking score was calculated by making [Z-scores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_score "Standard score") all datasets to standardize different data types on a common scale to better make comparisons among data.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Methodology-18)

The reputational component of the rankings (34.5 per cent of the overall score – 15 per cent for teaching and 19.5 per cent for research) came from an Academic Reputation Survey conducted by [Thomson Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomson_Reuters "Thomson Reuters") in spring 2010. The survey gathered 13,388 responses among scholars who, according to THE, were "statistically representative of global higher education's geographical and subject mix."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Methodology-18) However, the response rate of the survey in 2022-2024 was a mere 1.8%.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-22) The magazine's category for "industry income – innovation" came from a sole indicator, institution's research income from industry scaled against the number of academic staff." The magazine stated that it used this data as "proxy for high-quality knowledge transfer" and planned to add more indicators for the category in future years.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Methodology-18)

Data for [citation impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citation_impact "Citation impact") (measured as a normalized average citation per paper), comprising 32.5 per cent of the overall score, came from 12,000 [academic journals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_journal "Academic journal") [indexed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citation_index "Citation index") by Thomson Reuters' [Web of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_of_Science "Web of Science") database over the five years from 2004 to 2008. The *Times* stated that articles published in 2009–2010 have not yet completely accumulated in the database.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Methodology-18) The normalization of the data differed from the previous rankings system and is intended to "reflect variations in citation volume between different subject areas," so that institutions with high levels of research activity in the [life sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_science "Life science") and other areas with high citation counts will not have an unfair advantage over institutions with high levels of research activity in the [social sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_science "Social science"), which tend to use fewer citations on average.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Methodology-18)

The magazine announced on 5 September 2011 that its 2011–2012 World University Rankings would be published on 6 October 2011.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Launch_Date-23) At the same time, the magazine revealed changes to the ranking formula that will be introduced with the new rankings. The methodology will continue to use 13 indicators across five broad categories and will keep its "fundamental foundations," but with some changes. Teaching and research will each remain 30 per cent of the overall score, and industry income will remain at 2.5 per cent. However, a new "international outlook – staff, students and research" will be introduced and will make up 7.5 per cent of the final score. This category will include the proportion of international staff and students at each institution (included in the 2011–2012 ranking under the category of "international diversity"), but will also add the proportion of research papers published by each institution that are co-authored with at least one international partner. One 2011–2012 indicator, the institution's public research income, will be dropped.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-Launch_Date-23)

On 13 September 2011, the *Times Higher Education* announced that its 2011–2012 list will only rank the top 200 institutions. Phil Baty wrote that this was in the "interests of fairness," because "the lower down the tables you go, the more the data bunch up and the less meaningful the differentials between institutions become." However, Baty wrote that the rankings would include 200 institutions that fall immediately outside the official top 200 according to its data and methodology, but this "best of the rest" list from 201 to 400 would be unranked and listed alphabetically. Baty wrote that the magazine intentionally only ranks around 1 per cent of the world's universities in a recognition that "not every university should aspire to be one of the global research elite."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-24) However, the 2015/16 edition of the Times Higher Education World University Rankings ranks 800 universities, while Phil Baty announced that the 2016/17 edition, to be released on 21 September 2016, will rank "980 universities from 79 countries".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-26)

The methodology of the rankings was changed during the 2011–12 rankings process, with details of the changed methodology here.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-27) Phil Baty, the rankings editor, has said that the THE World University Rankings are the only global university rankings to examine a university's teaching environment, as others focus purely on research.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-28) Baty has also written that the THE World University Rankings are the only rankings to put arts and humanities and social sciences research on an equal footing to the sciences.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-29) However, this claim is no longer true. In 2015, QS introduced faculty area normalization to their QS World University Rankings, ensuring that citations data was weighted in a way that prevented universities specializing in the Life Sciences and Engineering from receiving undue advantage.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-30)

In November 2014, the magazine announced further reforms to the methodology after a review by parent company TES Global. The major change being all institutional data collection would be bought in house severing the connection with [Thomson Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomson_Reuters "Thomson Reuters"). In addition, research publication data would now be sourced from [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier "Elsevier")'s [Scopus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scopus "Scopus") database.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-announces-reforms-17)

### Reception

The reception to the methodology was varied.

Ross Williams of the [Melbourne Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Institute "Melbourne Institute"), commenting on the 2010–2011 draft, stated that the proposed methodology would favour more focused "science-based institutions with relatively few undergraduates" at the expense of institutions with more comprehensive programmes and undergraduates, but also stated that the indicators were "academically robust" overall and that the use of scaled measures would reward productivity rather than overall influence.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-praise1-5) [Steve Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Smith_(academic) "Steve Smith (academic)"), president of [Universities UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universities_UK "Universities UK"), praised the new methodology as being "less heavily weighted towards subjective assessments of reputation and uses more robust citation measures," which "bolsters confidence in the evaluation method."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-praise2-31) [David Willetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Willetts "David Willetts"), British [Minister of State for Universities and Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_for_Business,_Innovation_and_Skills "Department for Business, Innovation and Skills") praised the rankings, noting that "reputation counts for less this time, and the weight accorded to quality in teaching and learning is greater."[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-praise3-32) In 2014, David Willetts became chair of the TES Global Advisory Board, responsible for providing strategic advice to Times Higher Education.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-33)

### Criticism

Times Higher Education places a high importance on citations to generate rankings. Citations as a metric for effective education is problematic in many ways, placing universities who do not use English as their primary language at a disadvantage.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-34) Because English has been adopted as the international language for most academic societies and journals, citations and publications in a language different from English are harder to come across.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-35) Thus, such a methodology is criticized for being inappropriate and not comprehensive enough.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-RankingWatch-36) A second important disadvantage for universities of non-English tradition is that within the disciplines of social sciences and humanities the main tool for publications are books which are not or only rarely covered by digital citations records.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-37) In addition to these criticisms, the indicators used in the rankings have come under scrutiny. Several scholars, for example, have highlighted biases against [universities in the Arab region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education_in_the_Arab_world "Higher education in the Arab world") within existing rankings. They have advocated for the development of new methodologies that account for institutional disparities and ensure fair representation.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-39)

[Times Higher Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education "Times Higher Education") has also been criticized for its strong bias towards institutions that taught 'hard science' and had high quality output of research in these fields, often to the disadvantage of institutions focused on other subjects like the social sciences and humanities. For instance in the former [THE-QS World University Rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/THE-QS_World_University_Rankings "THE-QS World University Rankings"), the [London School of Economics (LSE)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_London_School_of_Economics_and_Political_Science "The London School of Economics and Political Science") was ranked 11th in the world in 2004 and 2005, but dropped to 66th and 67th in the 2008 and 2009 edition.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-40) In January 2010, THE concluded the method employed by [Quacquarelli Symonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quacquarelli_Symonds "Quacquarelli Symonds"), who conducted the survey on their behalf, was flawed in such a way that bias was introduced against certain institutions, including LSE.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-autogenerated4-41)

A representative of [Thomson Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomson_Reuters "Thomson Reuters"), THE's new partner, commented on the controversy: "*LSE stood at only 67th in the last Times Higher Education-QS World University Rankings – some mistake surely? Yes, and quite a big one*."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-autogenerated4-41) Nonetheless, after the change of data provider to Thomson Reuters the following year, LSE fell to 86th place, with the ranking described by a representative of Thomson Reuters as 'a fair reflection of their status as a world class university'.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-lse.ac.uk-42) [LSE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_School_of_Economics "London School of Economics") despite being ranked continuously near the top in its national rankings, has been placed below other British universities in the Times Higher Education World Rankings in recent years, other institutions such as [Sciences Po](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sciences_Po "Sciences Po") have suffered due to the inherent methodology bias still used.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] [Trinity College Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_College_Dublin "Trinity College Dublin")'s ranking in 2015 and 2016 was lowered by a basic mistake in data it had submitted; education administrator [Bahram Bekhradnia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahram_Bekhradnia?action=edit&redlink=1 "Bahram Bekhradnia (page does not exist)") said the fact this went unnoticed evinced a "very limited checking of data" "on the part of those who carry out such rankings". Bekhradnia also opined "while Trinity College was a respected university which could be relied upon to provide honest data, unfortunately that was not the case with all universities worldwide."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-43)

In general it is not clear who the rankings are made for. Many students, especially the undergraduate students, are not interested in the scientific work of a facility of higher education. Also the price of the education has no effects on the ranking. That means that private universities on the North American continent are compared to the European universities. Many European countries like France, Sweden or Germany for example have a long tradition on offering free education within facilities of higher education.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-45)

In 2021, the [University of Tsukuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tsukuba "University of Tsukuba") in [Ibaraki Prefecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibaraki_Prefecture "Ibaraki Prefecture"), Japan, was alleged to have submitted falsified data on the number of international students enrolled at the university to the Times Higher Education World University Rankings.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-universityworldnews.com-46) The discovery resulted in an investigation by THE and the provision of guidance to the university on the submission of data,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-universityworldnews.com-46) however, it also led to the criticism amongst faculty members of the ease with which THE's ranking system could be abused. The matter was discussed in Japan's National Diet on April 21, 2021.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-47)

Seven Indian Institutes of Technology (Mumbai, Delhi, Kanpur, Guwahati, Madras, Roorkee and Kharagpur) have boycotted THE rankings from 2020. These IITs have not participated in the rankings citing concerns over transparency.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-48) [Sorbonne University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorbonne_University "Sorbonne University")'s President [Nathalie Drach-Temam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathalie_Drach-Temam "Nathalie Drach-Temam") announced in October 2025 that they would no longer participate in the Times Higher Education rankings. [Zurich University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zurich_University "Zurich University") had already made a similar move. Drach-Temam criticised the rankings because the methodologies were not transparent and they could not be reproduced or questioned. She called them "black boxes" and noted they were run by commercial companies.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-norank-49)

## Regional rankings

### Asia

From 2013 to 2015, the outcomes of the *Times Higher Education* ***Asia University Rankings*** were the same as the Asian universities' position on its World University Rankings. In 2016, the Asia University Rankings was revamped and it "use the same 13 performance indicators as the THE World University Rankings, but have been recalibrated to reflect the attributes of Asia's institutions."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings#cite_note-THEAsia2016-82)

# Latin America University Rankings 2022

The *Times Higher Education* Latin America University Rankings is based on the same 13 rigorous performance indicators that underpin the *THE* World University Rankings, but the weightings differ to reflect the characteristics of Latin America’s universities. We evaluate universities across all their core missions: teaching, research, knowledge transfer and international outlook.

The 2022 ranking includes 197 institutions across 13 countries, up from 177 institutions last year. The Pontifical Catholic University of Chile is number one for the fourth consecutive year, while Brazil’s universities of São Paulo and Campinas hold on to second and third place respectively.

Argentina has a new top university, with Austral University in 44th place. University of the Andes remains Colombia’s best-performing university, at 13th. The highest new entry is Brazil’s Federal University of Paraíba, at 78th.

# Unifesp among Brazil’s Top Universities in THE World University Rankings 2025

**Unifesp** has once again secured its position among the **8 best universities in Brazil**, alongside leading institutions such as the University of São Paulo (USP), the University of Campinas (Unicamp), and the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ).

In the global ranking, **Unifesp** is positioned in the 801–1000 band among more than 2,000 universities evaluated across 115 countries, reaffirming its commitment to academic excellence and social impact. In subject-specific results, **Unifesp** achieved especially strong performance in several areas:

- **Clinical and Health Sciences**: ranked 301–400 worldwide, confirming its tradition of excellence in medical education and research.
- **Psychology**: ranked 401–500.
- **Education Studies**: ranked 401–500, showing its dedication to teacher training and educational research.
- **Life Sciences**: ranked 601–800, demonstrating strength in biological and environmental research.
- **Arts and Humanities**: ranked 601+, highlighting Unifesp's sucessful expansion into cultural and humanistic disciplines.
- **Social Sciences**: ranked 801–1000.
- **Computer Science**: ranked 801–1000.
- **Engineering**: ranked 1001–1250, representing the university’s ongoing development in the areas of Engineering, Computer Science, and Technology.
- **Physical Sciences**: ranked 1001+, and many others.

According to Professor Dr. Karen Spadari, these consistent results reflect “the university’s commitment to advancing knowledge, strengthening partnerships, and expanding its impact on Brazilian society and the world.”

**Unifesp**’s **International Outlook** has shown steady growth over recent years, reaching a score of 35.4 in the 2025 ranking. This consistent upward trend highlights the university’s ongoing efforts to build international partnerships, attract foreign students and researchers, and expand its global academic networks.

![](https://site.unifesp.br/sri/images/THE_international_index.png)

**Research** **Quality** at **Unifesp** has also shown highlights in recent years. The improvement demonstrates the university capacity to expand its academic excellence beyond teaching, positioning itself as a relevant global player in science and innovation.

![THE_research_index.png](https://site.unifesp.br/sri/images/THE_research_index.png)

Founded in 1933 as the Paulista School of Medicine, **Unifesp** has grown into a comprehensive federal university, with a mission to train health professionals, foster research, and promote social transformation. Over the past three decades, it has expanded beyond its São Paulo headquarters to establish campuses in Santos, Diadema, Guarulhos, São José dos Campos, and Osasco, offering more than 50 undergraduate and 70 graduate courses in a wide range of fields.

According to THE, the 2025 rankings analyzed over 2,000 universities from 115 countries, in one of the most in-depth surveys since 2004. **Unifesp**'s results reaffirm our dedication to high-quality education, research, and community engagement, building bridges between its medical legacy and new academic frontiers.

# Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp) | World University Rankings

São Paulo State University (UNESP), founded in 1976, is one of Brazil’s largest public universities with 24 campuses throughout the State of São Paulo.

Its multi-campus model allows UNESP to offer a varied academic programme with diverse activities. As one of Brazil’s foremost research universities, it cites subject strengths in health, engineering, communications, humanities, arts, social sciences and theoretical sciences.

UNESP is international recognised for the quality of its research, teaching and its initiatives to promote cultural diversity in the classroom. Its ethos emphasises critical thinking, humanist principles, sustainability, technological innovation and democratic participation in equal measures.

The university’s various campuses are also home to a diverse range of contemporary artworks, historical artefacts, farms, museums and a zoo, as well as hospitals and libraries.

São Paulo is Brazil’s wealthiest and most populous State, vibrant and cosmopolitan. Its capital, the city of São Paulo, is the country’s financial and cultural centre, home to a host of iconic architecture and events such as the São Paulo Art Biennial and the Brazilian Grand Prix. The city also hosts the largest LGBT Pride Festival in the world.

# Notícias Unesp - Unesp - Universidade Estadual Paulista

Por: ACI Unesp* e Comissão dos Rankings da Unesp

A última edição do World University Rankings, divulgado pela consultoria britânica Times Higher Education (THE), apontou a Unesp como a terceira melhor universidade do Brasil pela primeira vez desde 2004, quando o levantamento foi publicado pela primeira vez. Este levantamento da THE, especializada em ensino superior, é tido como um dos mais prestigiados do mundo para avaliar universidades em escala global.

Além do desempenho local, a evolução dos indicadores institucionais unespianos foi observada também no recorte mundial, em que a Universidade subiu para a faixa 601a-800a colocada, o mesmo patamar alcançado em 2023. Os principais destaques foram os crescimentos nos pilares "Ensino", da 277ª para a 210ª posição, "Ambiente de Pesquisa", da 416ª para a 346ª, e "Indústria", da 903ª para a 696ª --este último tem como subindicadores a captação de recursos com parceiros privados e o número de patentes, dialogando com o ecossistema de inovação da Unesp.

No World University Rankings, da Times Higher Education, as instituições mais bem avaliadas no Brasil foram a USP e a Unicamp. Empatadas em terceiro, com a mesma pontuação da Unesp, estão a Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ) e a Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS). No mundo, as melhores da lista foram, respectivamente, a Universidade de Oxford (Reino Unido), o MIT / Massachusetts Institute of Technology (Estados Unidos) e as universidades Princeton (EUA) e Cambridge (Reino Unido), que também empataram em terceiro. Harvard (EUA) é a quinta colocada.

Ao todo, foram incluídas no ranking da THE 2.191 instituições de ensino superior, sendo 59 brasileiras. O [resultado completo pode ser visto na página do THE World Ranking Universities](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/latest/world-ranking).

A melhora no desempenho institucional registrada no levantamento global da THE está em linha com o resultado recente observado regionalmente, e divulgado na semana passada, quando a Unesp alcançou a [sexta posição no QS World University Rankings: Latin America & The Caribbean](https://www2.unesp.br/portal#!/noticias/v/id::41644/ranking-aponta-unesp-como-sexta-melhor-da-america-latina). Este resultado mostrou uma ascensão constante dos indicadores unespianos nos últimos cinco anos e, assim como o resultado do THE, representou o melhor desempenho da Universidade no levantamento da QS focado na América Latina.

**Desempenho em alta**  
A nota final da Unesp nesta última edição do ranking ficou na faixa entre 39,0 e 43,5, uma melhora em comparação ao resultado do ano passado, quando a nota ficou entre 34,5 e 38,1. Para chegar ao resultado final, o THE World Ranking Universities avalia 18 indicadores divididos em cinco pilares: Ensino, Ambiente de Pesquisa, Qualidade da Pesquisa, Captação de Recursos e Perspectiva Internacional.

![](https://www2.unesp.br/Home/noticias8303/2025/10/41686/whatsapp-image-2025-10-08-at-72150-pm-1.jpeg)

Entre os cinco pilares avaliados pelo ranking, a Unesp apresentou desempenho superior à média nacional em “Ensino” e “Ambiente de Pesquisa”, dimensões que medem reputação e formação acadêmica, proporção de docentes por estudante, volume e financiamento de pesquisa e produtividade científica, entre outros indicadores. Em Ambiente de Pesquisa, o indicador Captação de Recursos subiu de 83,5 no ano passado para 99,7 nesta edição.

Nesse ponto específico, segundo dados compilados pela Pró-Reitoria de Pesquisa (ProPe) da Unesp, a Universidade ultrapassou o patamar de R$ 1 bilhão em recursos captados em projetos aprovados por agências de fomento (incluindo investimentos próprios, pagamentos de bolsas e parcerias via fundações) destinados a pesquisas científicas. Esse montante se refere ao quadriênio passado (2021-2024) e inclui recursos que ingressaram via Finep, CNPq, Fapesp, fundações ligadas à Unesp e programas institucionais, tais como os R$ 26 milhões destinados a editais de pós-doutorados de 2022 a 2024.

O indicador que se refere à Reputação em Pesquisa, embora tenha tido apenas uma leve alta no ranking da THE, alcançou um resultado importante em outro levantamento recente, publicado em setembro pela Elsevier, uma das maiores editoras científicas do mundo: 77 docentes e pesquisadores da Unesp foram classificados entre os 2% mais influentes do mundo em 2024, incluindo os pró-reitores de pós-graduação, Maria Valnice Boldrin, e de pesquisa, Edson Cocchieri Botelho. O resultado representa uma alta de 11,6% no número de professores da Unesp nessa [lista de excelência, que pode ser verificada na página da ProPe](https://www2.unesp.br/portal#!/prope/noticias/v/id::41627/pesquisadores-da-unesp-entre-os-mais-influentes-do-mundo).

**Investimento em ensino**  
No pilar "Ensino" do THE, foram registrados progressos nos indicadores que medem a "Proporção de Professores com Doutorado", cuja nota subiu de 78,5 no ano passado para 93,3 nesta edição, e nos investimentos institucionais, alta na nota de 69 para 82.

Nesse último item, pesaram a favor as 653 novas contratações para o quadro fixo de docentes da Universidade, ocorridas nos últimos três anos e meio, e a ampliação de políticas de inclusão e das formas de ingresso nos cursos de graduação da Unesp, que nos últimos anos abriram vagas adicionais para participantes de olimpíadas do conhecimento (olimpíadas científicas) e neste ano reservaram pela primeira vez vagas para um processo seletivo destinado a alunos que fizeram o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem).

Feito de acordo com as demandas de seu tempo, sob responsabilidade da Fundação para o Vestibular da Unesp (Vunesp), o Vestibular Unesp é historicamente um exame de números expressivos: em 46 edições, a seleção contabiliza mais de 3,4 milhões de inscritos para 260 mil vagas ofertadas desde 1981, já considerando as parciais de dados das [inscrições para o Vestibular Unesp 2026](https://www.vunesp.com.br/VNSP2504), encerradas nesta quarta-feira, 8 de outubro.

“Temos que avançar para que não percamos talentos. Na Unesp, temos os medalhistas como possibilidade de ingresso, agora vamos abrir para os atletas olímpicos, utilizamos agora o Enem pelo sistema universal, não só para vagas remanescentes. Assim conseguimos um ambiente mais plural que representa a totalidade do país. A autonomia (universitária) passa por isso, pelo diálogo com a sociedade, não pode ser um processo de isolamento”, disse a reitora Maysa Furlan no [evento “A Autonomia Universitária, a Pós-Graduação e os Impactos da Universidade Pública Brasileira”](https://www2.unesp.br/portal#!/noticias/v/id::41680/gestores-das-universidades-publicas-paulistas-e-agencias-de-fomento-se-reunem-para-discutir-autonomia), realizado esta semana em São Paulo.

![](https://www2.unesp.br/Home/noticias8303/2025/10/41686/whatsapp-image-2025-10-08-at-72150-pm.jpeg)

Na avaliação da Comissão de Rankings da Unesp, o avanço observado nos resultados do THE World University Rankings demonstra o compromisso permanente da Unesp com a excelência acadêmica e com a produção de conhecimento voltada para o desenvolvimento científico, tecnológico e social do Estado de São Paulo e do país. Mais detalhes sobre a [metodologia usada pelo World University Ranking pode ser vista na página oficial](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/methodology).

**A Unesp e os rankings**  
A Comissão dos Rankings da Unesp esclarece que os resultados de rankings não representam os objetivos da instituição, nem a visão de futuro da Universidade, com elevado grau de comprometimento com a pesquisa aplicada às realidades de transformação das condições socioeconômicas e ambientais do Estado de São Paulo e de modo geral do Brasil. Os resultados, entretanto, são relevantes porque mostram as consequências das ações que são realizadas continuamente pela Universidade.

---

**Com a colaboração da assessoria de imprensa da Fundação Vunesp*

Unesp, USP e Unicamp lideram as universidades brasileiras em Ranking Mundial

Segundo o Ranking a “UNESP é o modelo de universidade multicampi de maior sucesso no Brasil”

---

 ![](https://alumni.unesp.br/images/1207961572/logo_1600206180717.jpg)

O *Ranking of World Universities* - ARWU (Ranking Acadêmico das Universidades Mundiais) de 2020 existe desde 2003 e é considerado como um dos rankings mais confiáveis e transparentes do mundo. Todo ano, o ARWU seleciona 2 mil universidades, mas apenas as mil melhores são divulgadas por ele. Neste ano, as faculdades brasileiras foram lideradas pela USP, UNESP e Unicamp.

A análise das universidades é feita pelo CWCU - Center for World-Class Universities (Centro para Universidades de Classe Mundial), do Instituto de Educação Superior de Shanghai, na China. Segundo o jornal The Economist é "a classificação anual mais usada, sobre universidades de pesquisa, do mundo".

O Brasil teve 22 universidades reconhecidas pelo ARWU, todas são instituições públicas, sendo 18 instituições federais e 4 estaduais. Este é o primeiro ano em que três universidades estaduais paulistas são as primeiras colocadas brasileiras. A primeira da lista foi a Universidade de São Paulo (USP) que aparece entre as posições 101-150, em seguida estão empatadas a UNESP e a Unicamp que aparecem entre 301-400 da classificação global, as três federais seguintes ocupam a faixa entre 401-500.

O ARWU divulgou em seu [site oficial](http://www.shanghairanking.com/World-University-Rankings/UNESP.html) que a UNESP “é o modelo de universidade multicampus de maior sucesso no Brasil. Essa característica única permite atividades intensas e diversificadas em São Paulo. Sua influência pode ser reconhecida pelo nível de desenvolvimento regional onde estão localizados seus campi: um na capital paulista e 22 outros estrategicamente distribuídos pelo estado. Consolidou-se como um projeto que une o desenvolvimento científico, tecnológico, econômico, cultural e social comprometido com os princípios democráticos e claramente consciente de sua condição de instituição governamental, inserida e fortemente atuante na sociedade brasileira”.

Além disso, no site da ARWU afirma-se que “seu alto nível de qualificação pode ser comprovado pelo expressivo número de ex-alunos inseridos no mercado profissional, bem como sua posição de destaque no ranking nacional brasileiro em todas as áreas em que atua, seguindo a tendência mundial e, com a certeza, de estar preparada para isso. A Unesp está agora, mais do que nunca, em busca de novas fronteiras a cruzar e desafios a enfrentar, firmando novos convênios com Instituições de primeira linha em todo o mundo. A UNESP é uma instituição respeitada com membros talentosos, programas totalmente credenciados e forte base de pesquisa - e essas continuarão sendo suas prioridades. A UNESP é uma das maiores e mais importantes universidades brasileiras, com destacadas realizações em ensino, pesquisa e extensão em serviços”.

Como metodologia para a avaliação, o ARWU possui indicadores principais: o número dos pesquisadores mais citados; o número de artigos publicados nas revistas Nature e Science; o número de artigos indexados no Science Citation Index – Expanded e no Social Sciences Citation Index; o desempenho de pesquisa per capita relativo ao tamanho da instituição; o número de ex-alunos e funcionários vencedores de prêmios Nobel e de premiações em suas áreas.

Para ter acesso a lista completa e mais informações sobre o Ranking acesse este [link](http://www.shanghairanking.com/).

The **Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária*, abbreviated **MAPA**) is a [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") department in Brazil. The jurisdiction of this ministry is to formulate and implement policies for [agribusiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agribusiness "Agribusiness") development, integrating the aspects of market, technological, organizational and environmental care for the consumers of the country and abroad, promoting [food security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_security "Food security"), income generation and employment, reducing inequalities and increasing social inclusion.

The Ministry was founded during the [Brazilian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Empire "Brazilian Empire") in 1860. Originally named *Secretaria de Estado dos Negócios da Agricultura, Comércio e Obras Públicas*, the body was extinguished in the early years of the [First Brazilian Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Brazilian_Republic "First Brazilian Republic") and re-established in 1906 as the *Ministerio dos Negocios da Agricultura, Industria e Commercio*.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-2) In 1930, it was renamed the *Ministério da Agricultura*.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-3) From 2001–2022 it was the *Ministério da Agricultura, Pecuária e Abastecimento*, from which the acronym MAPA derives.

## Agroenergy

Brazil is the world leader in producing agroenergy and the Ministry of Agriculture encourages policies which develop [ethanol fuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethanol_fuel "Ethanol fuel") production.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-4)
